stories.headline: Sakana AI launches Fugu, a multi-agent orchestrator that behaves like a single model

key_facts.fact: Japanese startup Sakana AI publicly released Fugu on Monday, a multi-agent orchestration system delivered as a single foundation model accessible through one OpenAI-compatible API; it ships in two variants, Fugu and Fugu Ultra.
key_facts.excerpt: Japanese startup Sakana AI announced Monday the public release of the Sakana Fugu service that combines multiple artificial intelligence models into one collaborative workflow.

key_facts.fact: Rather than being a standalone model, Fugu dynamically routes queries to a swappable pool of specialized AI agents, deciding whether to answer directly or assemble and coordinate a team of expert models internally.
key_facts.excerpt: Fugu (Japanese for 'pufferfish'), bypasses the traditional monolithic model structure by dynamically routing queries to a swappable pool of specialized AI agents.

key_facts.fact: Sakana says Fugu Ultra exceeds Claude Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench (Fugu Ultra 93.2, Fugu 92.9, Fable 89.8) and beats Mythos Preview on GPQA-Diamond (Fugu Ultra 95.5, Mythos Preview 94.6), claiming parity with frontier models without export-control exposure.
key_facts.excerpt: Fugu actually exceeds the performance of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench (Fugu Ultra: 93.2, Fugu: 92.9, Fable: 89.8), and beats the prior Claude Mythos Preview model on GPQA-D (Fugu Ultra: 95.5, Fugu: 95.5, Mythos Preview: 94.6).

key_facts.fact: Sakana frames Fugu as a hedge against vendor lock-in and export controls, noting access to top models 'can disappear overnight' and that orchestrating a swappable agent pool routes around vendor restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: Relying on a single company's model for national infrastructure is a massive risk. As recent export controls have shown, access to top models can disappear overnight... Fugu simply routes around vendor restrictions by relying on an entirely swappable agent pool.

key_facts.fact: Fugu Ultra went live on Vercel's AI Gateway as 'sakana/fugu-ultra' on Monday, June 22.
key_facts.excerpt: Our Fugu models surpass publicly accessible frontier models and are shoulder-to-shoulder with Fable 5 and Mythos Preview in various rigorous engineering, scientific, and reasoning benchmarks while delivering frontier capability without the risk of export controls.

stories.headline: SpaceX signs up-to-$6.3B compute deal with open-source lab Reflection AI at Colossus 2

key_facts.fact: SpaceX signed a computing-power agreement with open-source AI startup Reflection AI on Monday, granting immediate access to Nvidia GB300 chips at the Colossus 2 data center near Memphis, Tennessee.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX has signed a major computing power deal with Reflection AI for access to Nvidia GB300 chips at Elon Musk's Colossus 2 data center.

key_facts.fact: Reflection will pay $150 million per month beginning July 1, 2026 through 2029, with payments totaling about $6.3 billion if the deal runs its full term.
key_facts.excerpt: The open-source AI startup will pay Musk's company $150 million per month starting July 1, 2026, with payments totaling about $6.3 billion if the deal runs through 2029.

key_facts.fact: Either company can terminate the contract with 90 days' notice after the first three months.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is worth up to $6.3 billion and either company has the option to end the contract with 90 days' notice after the first three months.

key_facts.fact: The Reflection deal is smaller than SpaceX's earlier Colossus deals with Anthropic ($1.25 billion/month) and Google ($920 million/month), both also running through July 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is smaller than SpaceX's deals with Anthropic and Google, which cost the companies $1.25 billion per month and $920 million per month, respectively.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia-backed Reflection AI, valued at $25 billion and founded in 2024 by two former Google DeepMind researchers, said the additional compute lets it accelerate 'American open intelligence'; the move follows the U.S. government's ban on Anthropic's closed Fable and Mythos models for foreign nationals.
key_facts.excerpt: Open-weight AI models... have received more attention following the U.S. government's ban of Anthropic's closed models, Fable and Mythos. The startup, which was founded in 2024 by two former Google DeepMind researchers...

stories.headline: OpenAI releases full GPT-5.5-Cyber and launches Patch the Planet with Trail of Bits

key_facts.fact: On Monday, OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cybersecurity program with Patch the Planet, an initiative founded with Trail of Bits (in collaboration with HackerOne and Calif) to help open-source maintainers move from vulnerability findings to deployed fixes.
key_facts.excerpt: Patch the Planet is an initiative built to help maintainers move from findings to fixes. Founded with Trail of Bits, and in collaboration with HackerOne and Calif, we are funding expert security researchers and equipping them with Codex Security and our advanced models.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI released a full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber, its security-specialized model, scoring 85.6% on the CyberGym benchmark versus 81.8% for standard GPT-5.5; access stays restricted to vetted defenders through its Trusted Access for Cyber program.
key_facts.excerpt: The full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber also went live, replacing a permissive-only preview. OpenAI put its CyberGym score at 85.6%, up from 81.8% for the standard GPT-5.5.

key_facts.fact: More than 30 open-source projects have committed to participate, with initial participants including cURL, Go, Python, Sigstore and pyca/cryptography.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 30 open-source projects have committed to participate, with initial participants including cURL, Go, Python, Sigstore, and pyca/cryptography.

key_facts.fact: In its first week, Patch the Planet produced hundreds of discovered bugs, 64 pull requests and 51 issues filed across 19 projects, with Trail of Bits putting its entire security research organization on the effort.
key_facts.excerpt: The impact is hundreds of discovered bugs, 64 pull requests, and 51 issues filed across 19 projects (with many more still undergoing coordinated disclosure). That was just the first week of Patch the Planet.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI cited Linux Foundation and Harvard research that 94% of widely used projects studied had fewer than 10 developers responsible for over 90% of code, and said a human security engineer reviews every Patch the Planet finding before it reaches a maintainer.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI cited research from the Linux Foundation and Harvard finding that 94% of the widely used projects studied had fewer than 10 developers responsible for more than 90% of the code added in a year... a human security engineer reviews every Patch the Planet finding before it reaches a maintainer.

stories.headline: Groq raises $650M to scale its AI inference cloud after Nvidia licensing deal

key_facts.fact: Groq announced $650 million in new growth capital on Monday, June 22, led by Disruptive and Infinitum, to accelerate expansion of its AI inference cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: Groq, Inc. today announced $650 million in new growth capital to accelerate the expansion of its AI inference cloud. The round was led by Disruptive and Infinitum, with participation from investors who elected to reinvest in the company.

key_facts.fact: The raise follows a December 2025 non-exclusive licensing deal with Nvidia, reported at $20 billion, in which Nvidia hired away founder/CEO Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra and other staff; investors were paid out and asked to reinvest.
key_facts.excerpt: The raise comes roughly six months after Nvidia signed a non-exclusive licensing agreement for Groq's technology and hired away founder and CEO Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra, and other employees.

key_facts.fact: Groq did not disclose its new valuation; it was last valued at $6.9 billion following a $750 million round in September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Groq did not disclose its new valuation. It was last valued at $6.9 billion following a $750 million round in September.

key_facts.fact: The company plans to scale toward 200 MW of inference capacity by the end of 2027, fitting out its footprint with Nvidia's new LPX inference system.
key_facts.excerpt: expects to scale toward 200 MW by the end of 2027... capital accelerates the fit-out of its existing footprint with Groq's latest inference technology, including the new LPX system from NVIDIA.

stories.headline: AppsFlyer raises over $1B from Google, Meta, Unity and Moloco at $2.7B valuation

key_facts.fact: Ad-measurement firm AppsFlyer raised more than $1 billion in Series E funding at a $2.7 billion post-money valuation, with Moloco, Google, Meta and Unity each acquiring a minority stake.
key_facts.excerpt: AppsFlyer has raised more than $1 billion in Series E funding at a $2.7 billion post-money valuation... Moloco, Google, Meta and Unity have each acquired a minority stake in AppsFlyer.

key_facts.fact: CEO and co-founder Oren Kaniel said the investments are minority, non-controlling, non-exclusive, and that each investor is integrated with AppsFlyer but will not receive preferential treatment; the transaction is subject to regulatory approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: The investments are non-exclusive and while each company is integrated with AppsFlyer, they will not receive preferential treatment, he says. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals.

key_facts.fact: AppsFlyer said it will use the capital to accelerate AI-powered advertising measurement, cross-platform attribution and infrastructure to support autonomous marketing and AI-driven workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: AppsFlyer said it intends to use the capital to accelerate innovation in AI-powered advertising measurement, advance cross-platform attribution and measurement capabilities, and continue building infrastructure designed to support autonomous marketing and AI-driven workflows.

key_facts.fact: The San Francisco-based company works with more than 15,000 brands, has about 1,300 employees, and had previously raised $300 million, including a 2020 General Atlantic-led Series D of $210 million at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: The SF-based company works with more than 15,000 brands globally and has about 1,300 employees. The company has previously raised $300 million. Its General Atlantic-led 2020 Series D was $210 million at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation.

stories.headline: Five Eyes cyber agencies warn frontier AI will transform hacking 'in months, not years'

key_facts.fact: On Monday, the cyber security agencies of the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand issued a rare joint three-page statement warning that frontier AI is rapidly transforming cyber risk and that leaders must act swiftly.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Frontier AI models are anticipated to exceed current industry expectations, fundamentally transforming both offensive and defensive cyber capabilities,' the intelligence alliance commonly known as the Five Eyes said in a three-page statement on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The statement said the timeline for AI-supercharged offensive cyber capabilities 'is not years, it is months,' urging leaders to prioritize foundational security controls and integrate AI into their defenses.
key_facts.excerpt: Frontier Al models are anticipated to exceed current industry expectations, fundamentally transforming both offensive and defensive cyber capabilities. The timeline is not years, it is months.

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported the warning reflects officials' growing concern over models such as Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber, said to let users execute complex and potentially devastating hacks.
key_facts.excerpt: The warning was another indication of officials' increasing concerns over models such as Anthropic's Mythos or OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber, which are said to allow users to quickly execute complex - and potentially devastating - hacks.

key_facts.fact: The statement follows the US government ordering Anthropic to disable a version of Mythos for foreign nationals, and CISA - a co-signer - cutting deadlines for officials to fix serious vulnerabilities to three days, citing AI threats.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic was forced to disable a version of Mythos after the US government ordered it to suspend access to the models for foreign nationals... the US cyber-defence agency, CISA, which was among those co-signing Monday's statement, reduced the deadlines imposed on government officials to deal with serious digital vulnerabilities in their networks to three days.

stories.headline: Oracle says AI adoption helped cut 21,000 jobs in past year, per annual filing

key_facts.fact: In an annual regulatory filing on Monday, June 22, Oracle disclosed its global workforce fell by 21,000 to 141,000 full-time employees as of May 31, 2026, down from 162,000 a year earlier - roughly a 13% cut.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle reduced its workforce by 13% over the past 12 months and cited AI deployment in an annual filing on Monday. The company currently employs 141,000 full-time workers, down from 162,000 the previous year.

key_facts.fact: Oracle's filing stated that 'the adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce,' Oracle said on Monday (Jun 22) in an annual financial regulatory filing.

key_facts.fact: The cuts led to about $1.8 billion in severance and restructuring costs over the past year, up sharply from a $374 million restructuring bill the prior year.
key_facts.excerpt: The firm said the cuts have led to about $1.8bn (£1.36bn) in severance payments and other restructuring costs in the past year... The sum is significantly higher than the $374m restructuring bill in the previous financial year.

key_facts.fact: The reductions come as Oracle faces financial pressure from an expensive build-out of AI data centers for customers such as OpenAI and Meta; the company joins peers whose collective AI capex plans could reach $700 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle joins several tech giants, including Meta, Google, Microsoft and Amazon, who have announced capex plans that could reach $700 billion to fuel their AI data center developments.
